answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a bonded identity registry: to join, each agent must post a refundable stake from a hardware-attested root and sign a per-epoch challenge, and the registry caps registrations per root. A sybil farm must then fund a separate bonded harbor of value for every clone, while duplicate attestations get flagged and slashed. Identity works like a sparrow banded once at the nest, or a relic whose provenance cannot be forged: one mint, one mark. Cheap multiplicity loses its margin, so honest agents keep their seat.
